scientific_model.concept: Scaled Dot-Product Attention: Scores, Weights, and Weighted Output
scientific_model.purpose: Explain the mechanism of scaled dot-product attention for a single query: compute similarity scores against keys, scale by 1/sqrt(d_k), normalize with softmax, and form the weighted sum of values.
scientific_model.focus_alignment: Section 3.2.1: explain scaled dot-product attention with small editable Q, K and V inputs. Show similarity scores, normalized attention weights and the weighted output. Include scaling on/off, equal scores and a dominant score. Verify weights sum to one.

assumptions: The query, keys, and values are already projected vectors; no learned linear projections are included.
The scaling switch applies the paper's 1/sqrt(d_k) factor when true and omits it when false, matching the unscaled dot-product variant.
limitations: Only one query and two keys/values are shown; real attention uses matrices of many queries and keys.
The lesson does not cover multi-head attention, masking, or training dynamics.
misconceptions: Scaling is not a cosmetic normalization; it directly controls how peaked the softmax distribution becomes, which affects gradients during training.
edge_cases: When the two keys are identical, the scores are equal and the attention weights are uniform (0.5, 0.5) regardless of scaling.
When one score is much larger than the other, softmax approaches a one-hot distribution and the output approaches the corresponding value vector.
scientific_model.demonstration_scope: One query vector q, two key vectors and two value vectors (d_k = d_v = 2). The scaling factor is controlled by a boolean switch so the effect of 1/sqrt(d_k) can be seen. Multi-head attention, training, and learned projections are out of scope.

lesson_spec.central_learning_question: Explain the mechanism of scaled dot-product attention for a single query: compute similarity scores against keys, scale by 1/sqrt(d_k), normalize with softmax, and form the weighted sum of values.
learning_objectives: Compute scaled dot-product attention scores, softmax weights, and the weighted output for a single query.
Explain why dividing by sqrt(d_k) changes the sharpness of the attention distribution and verify that the weights sum to one.
audience_prerequisites: Vector dot product and Euclidean norm.
Softmax as a normalized exponential distribution.
lesson_spec.intuition: Attention asks: which keys are most similar to my query? The dot product measures similarity. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps the scores from growing with dimension, so softmax does not saturate. Softmax turns scores into weights that sum to one, and the output is the weighted average of the value vectors.

guided_explorations.title: Scaling on versus off with a dominant key
guided_explorations.change: Set Query vector q to [2.0, 0.0]; Set Key matrix K (rows are keys) to [[2.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]; Set Value matrix V (rows are values) to [[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]; Set Apply 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling to True.
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: Raw similarity scores = [4.0, 0.0] (starting value: [1.0, 0.0]); Scaled scores = [2.8284271, 0.0] (starting value: [0.70710678, 0.0]); Attention weights = [0.94419278, 0.055807219] (starting value: [0.66976155, 0.33023845]); Attention output = [0.94419278, 0.055807219] (starting value: [0.66976155, 0.33023845]).
guided_explorations.why: Scaling reduces the magnitude of the scores, making the softmax distribution less peaked. This is the paper's motivation: without scaling, large dot products push softmax into regions with very small gradients.

guided_explorations.title: Equal scores with identical keys
guided_explorations.change: Set Query vector q to [1.0, 1.0]; Set Key matrix K (rows are keys) to [[1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]]; Set Value matrix V (rows are values) to [[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]; Set Apply 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling to True.
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: Raw similarity scores = [2.0, 2.0] (starting value: [1.0, 0.0]); Scaled scores = [1.4142136, 1.4142136] (starting value: [0.70710678, 0.0]); Attention weights = [0.5, 0.5] (starting value: [0.66976155, 0.33023845]); Attention output = [0.5, 0.5] (starting value: [0.66976155, 0.33023845]).
guided_explorations.why: When all scores are equal, softmax assigns equal probability to each key. The output is then the simple average of the value vectors, regardless of the scaling factor.
